prose.text: The chunk's own probes come first, then the targeted pins, then the builds the legs need, the swap and three local legs, then the standard gate set in test-plan §3 order (`capability-drift` before the default-features workspace nextest, the `--features mcp-server` bindings regen as the last cargo-adjacent step, the base-identity bindings close, since the chunk adds no procedure), then the local pre-push check, then the operator pass.

The three legs boot the release app on this host under a virtual display. Each moves the receivers to 14317 and 14318 through the two port variables, so the shared ports 4317 and 4318 are never bound; each unsets `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`; each writes a fresh data dir under `target/`, named at invocation. The boot verb rebuilds the release binary itself, so the legs read the tree as it stands. They are the boot-path smoke test-plan §3 asks for when `pulse-app/src/main.rs` changes, in its harness `boot` form.

- **The close leg** runs eight boots with the runner's Xlib swapped in. At the base it reads `self-ended` (P3: 6   of 8, 8 of 8 and 5 of 8 in three series). The swap is the fetch entry's two libraries named through   `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` on that one command. The `ldd` entry before it is its known positive: without it a green leg   could be the host's own Xlib. The `ldd` entry after the legs reads the swap gone. - **The repair leg** boots once with no display at all, so the app ends before ready by itself (P4 reading:   `app ended: exit 101`, witness label `runtime-exit`), then runs a series of one boot in the same data dir. At   the base the series lists no ordinal 1. That boot's log holds a panic record by design; no gate grades it. - **The host leg** is the prior chunk's series of two on the host's own Xlib, unchanged. - A before-ready self-end of a series boot (ordinal 2 and up) has no local leg: nothing on this host makes the app   end before ready on demand under a live display. Step 2's fixture pin and the repair leg, which drives the same   read on a real process, stand for it. On the runner it is read only if a self-end recurs.

Absences, each with its reason: - No webview gate and no headful self-verify: no `pulse-app/ui/**` path is touched and no rendered surface   changes. The `a11y` job's verdict is read from the operator pass's run; its regression reading compares against   a base download that has no producer in any workflow (a11y-plan amendment `2026-10-09-ci-on-linux-alone`, Kept),   so the criterion below asks for the job's own conclusion and artifacts, not a base diff. - No Windows leg and no `agent-run.ps1` edit: nothing runs it here or in CI. - No retry anywhere. The two re-runs of the operator pass are not retries of a red: each is fired only while every   attempt before it read no self-end, each is one more reading of the stated three, and a self-end in any attempt   stops the pass and is the reading.

The files a CI run keeps (`logs/boot-series.json`, `logs/harness-settled.json`, `logs/exit-witness.jsonl`, `logs/series/boot-{ordinal}/`) are produced by that run, a step outside this block; the operator pass's read entries carry no `artifact`.

**The operator pass, in this order.** 1. The hygiene entry, the pre-CI commit, the local pre-push check, then the build-branch push. 2. The CI read of the pushed tip, asserted green. It is attempt 1 and the chunk's CI verdict. 3. Three reads of that attempt by the run's id: its jobs (report-only), the `boot` job's log lines with the    `ci-gates` frame line, and the run's `logs-boot-Linux` artifact with the series verdict, the smoke's settle    verdict, every witness file whole and the merge commit its log carries. 4. **Each kept witness file is read whole.** A line holding anything beyond its shape stops the pass, and the    operator is told. 5. **The stop at a self-end.** If any boot of an attempt ended by itself, the pass stops. Nothing is re-run and    nothing is fixed on top. The report says what the job kept for that boot (its ordinal, its exit record, its    `exit_witness` label, its witness lines whole) and that the close is not shown; P-129 is not verified. 6. When attempt 1 holds no self-end: the `boot` job alone is re-run on the same commit, and attempt 2 is read the    same way; when attempt 2 holds none, once more for attempt 3. Every attempt is recorded with its number, its    merge commit and its artifact id, and none replaces another. 7. A red in any other job is the standard pass's: read its log, fix on top with a further commit, read again.    Then the count of three starts over on the new commit, since the source changed.
Evidence files are written by /implement and by the operator pass from the entries' recorded outputs; no entry writes one.
